Permit API: 051-24210
Unconventional: Yes
County: Fayette
Municipality: Nicholson Township

Inspection Date: 4/15/2025
Comments: On April 15 2025, the Department conducted a routine partial inspection of the Kovalic 13 Well Site.Upon inspection, it appears that an erosion channel has formed in the area of previous excavation and backfill. The erosion channel appears to start just downslope of the well head, and travels the full length of the backfilled area. The Department observed sediment deposited in the vegetated area where the erosion channel terminated. The Department did not observe any E and S BMPs installed on/around the site. The Department recommends the operator promptly ensure the site is properly stabilized and install E and S BMPs to prevent further migration of sediment and to minimize the potential for further sedimentation tooccur.Prior to leaving the site the Department contacted operator representative Heather Empfield to inform her of the observations made by the Department.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for failure to properly temporarily stabilize the site and failure to implement E and S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.Transmittal of this inspection is delayed due to an IT app error.

Unconventional: No

Inspection Date: 10/29/2024
Comments: Department received application for transfer of well permits for the Hickman Speerstra #5 well located in Venango County, Cranberry Township. Photo#1. Transfer has not yet been approved from PENNFIELD ENERGY, LLC. to LAKESHORE ENERGY DEVELOPMENT, LLC. Onsite to complete inspection before application approval. API 121-45712. Confirmed Coordinates. Well is equipped with rods, inside 2" tubing, inside 6-1/4" casing. Photos #2/#3. The casing and tubing are both open to the atmosphere. No venting detected at time of inspection. Photo #3. No pump jack is on well, and no production line is coming off the well. No label was attached to the well. No posting was observed on or near the location. On location was a vertical steel tank inside a plastic lined earthen dike. Photo #4. Also on location was a disabled track mounted service rig. Photo #5. No production records were found for 2023. Production reported to the Department for 2022 was 100 mcf gas for 120 days. No oil reported. No MIA records were found for 2023 or 2022. MIA reported to the Department for 2021 has 8 psi on primary production string with no corrosion. No fluid or gas leaks detected on site at the time of inspection. The condition of the well at the time of inspection shows it is inoperable and unable to produce. Well is considered abandoned. The operator is in violation of: OGA 3211(G) Well Permits-Posting OGA 3211(H) Well Permits-Labeling 78.88(E)-Mechanical Integrity of Operating Wells 78.121(A)-Well Production Reporting OGA 3220(A)- Abandoned Well. OGA 3216 (C)- Equipment not being used for production.

The findings were as follows:According to the Order issued to the operator by the Department for this site, the Operator shall completely restore the well site within 9 months after plugging.The well site was not restored during today's inspection. The site was not exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. According to the landowner, the site has not been restored to pre-existing contours.The well was plugged on October 7, 2021 according the the plugging certificate submitted by the Operator for this well. Although there has been additional growth since the Department's last inspection in July of 2023, lack of adequate uniform vegetation is still observed due to multiple areas of exposed soil and rock. There are several bare spots throughout the former well site that are lacking adequate uniform vegetation. No E and S BMPs are installed on site.The ground appears to be seeded in most areas, but 70% uniform vegetation has not been achieved at this time. Vegetative growth may be hindered by the amount of rock and gravel on site. The Department recommends the Operator take necessary measures to ensure 70% uniform vegetative growth is achieved for restoration of the site.Based on today's inspection, violations shall remain outstanding.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 2019-01-30
Comments: WQS Gene Rickard and I performed an INCDT inspection of the Mitchell well site regarding a reported release which occurred aroung 0830 on Jan. 30, 2019. The complaint number was 339494. The release was reported to me via Briana Cunningham, WQSS. Other individuals on site were Mike Deming and Mr. Otten of Southwestern Energy Production Co. The weather at the time of inspection was around 15 degrees F and snowing. Wind was gusting. At about 0830 hrs. a tank in the onsite tank battery was being filled from a production fluid tank. The operator allegedly was monitoring the tank level from the hatch nearest the front part of the tank. According to a relayed assessment, the operator thought the tank was positioned not quite level, allowing the fluid level to overflow the back part of the tank, spilling onto the containment area surrounding the battery. The containment was later found to be compromised and allowed water to leave the containment area. SWN notified the Department on 1/30/2019. According to onsite representatives, approximately 5-6 bbls. of produced water were released to containment, then through the compromised liner to the pad surface. Resource Environmental was called in to delineate the impacted area, and has been directing a dewatering action to mitigate the impact until the tank battery can be moved, as the tanks are currently frozen to the ground. The timeframe for moving the tanks to delineate the affected area appears to be over the weekend. While onsite, crews were attempting to locate any tears in containment, which was being hampered by the icy buildup inside the containment. Workers were also mobilizing tankers to dewater the area and tanks in the tank battery in preparation for movement off containment to allow resource to delineate the affected area. The affected area seems to stop about 10' from the berm, according to test pits dug for assessment. The spill will be going to Act 2. SWN Representative Mike Deming said a possible change in protocol from a 6" to a 12" tank freeboard is being considered. Violations are attached.

Violation ID: 8213982
Permit API: 051-24701
Unconventional: Yes
County: Fayette
Municipality: German Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 1/13/2025
Comments: On January 13, 2025, the Department conducted an Incident Inspection of EQT's Herriott Well Pad after a spill was reported to the emergency hotline at 1:50pm on January 12, 2025. According to the spill report and a verbal conversation with Logan Dominick of EQT via the phone, at 1pm on 1/12/2025, a truck drove over a hose breaking the coupling on the hose releasing production fluids. Mr. Dominick stated that 90% of the spill occurred on containment and approximately 10% spilled off of containment. Mr. Dominick estimated that 10 gallons spilled and stated that SPSI scraped approximately 6 inches of the well pad in the spill area as well as vacuumed up the containment and placed all contaminated materials into a dumpster on site.At the time of this inspection EQT representative Jeremy Barber was on site and inform the Department that Flowback was currently occurring. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a section of the pad that was scrapped adjacent to two frack tanks that were in containment. The Department also observed a dumpster adjacent to the spill area. In the middle of the spill area appeared to be a strip of containment that had hoses in it. Mr. Barber pointed out that the open hose was the one that was ran over and caused the spill. The Department did not observe any holes or tears in the hose containment or the frack tank containment and the containments appeared to be dry.Background conductivity readings were taken adjacent to the well pad on the perimeter and some vegetation (0.289mS) and then readings were taken in the spill area that was scraped (0.0945 mS, 0.0386, 0.0416mS), then a reading was taken outside but directly adjacent to the spill area (0.0036 mS). Mr. Barber informed the Department that the area underneath these containments had not been scraped yet and that as soon as Flowback is completed, they will be pulled, the area beneath them will be scraped, and any contaminated material will be properly disposed of. The Department took conductivity readings at the edge/underneath this containment to determine if this area is contaminated, and the readings are as follows: 3.34 mS and 1.649 under/adjacent to the containment of the frack tanks where the spill occurred, and 13.98 mS under/adjacent to the containment where the hose is and where the spill originated. The soil conductivity readings in the spill area where the ground has been scraped, is comparable to the background reading and therefore appears to be remediated in accordance with the Department's policy for small spills, however, the readings in the area at the edge of/underneath the containment lining were elevated compared to the background reading and therefore appears to still be contaminated. The Department verbally recommended to Mr. Barber that the containment be lifted and materials be scraped as soon as possible. Mr. Barber informed The Department that SPSI will be back on site today and they will continue to remediate the release in accordance with policies. Mr. Barber also stated that photo documentation of continued remediate efforts will be supplied to the Department as soon as it is available. The Department is requesting the Operator submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release. The Department is requesting how the Operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Based on today's inspection and the spill not being completely remediated yet, violations are being issued for an approximately 10 gallon release of production fluid from a hose onto the well pad.

Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted in order to assess conditions on Pad B after the 12/19/22 reported produced fluid release from the MASS to the northeast corner of the pad surface as well as to the north stormwater channel. I met with Ian of EQT during this inspection on Pad B. I spoke with a representative with EQT's contracted consulting group, Creston Environmental. The frac is still staged on Pad B.The area of the pad surface where the release occurred remains damp but no standing water was observed. A lined sump was constructed at the east outlet of the north stormwater channel. Fluid was observed slowly flowing into the sump. The electrical conductivity of this fluid was approximately 16 mS/cm. The channel and pad side slopes remain snow-covered. A work crew began removing the remaining snow from the northeast corner of the pad where the release occurred at the beginning of this inspection.Later in this inspection Sam Louderback and Amber Boyd from the DEP ECB program joined me on Pad B. The work crew then began attempting to dig a trench at the northeast corner of the pad but did not make very much progress. Six wells remain in production on Pad A. Six GPUs are present and appear to be in good condition. Some equipment for the frac is staged on Pad A.Violations remain outstanding for the 12/19/22 reported release of produced fluid on Pad B.

Comments: On December 15, 2023, I conducted an inspection of the WL Hopkins Well Site. The inspection was conducted in response to a request made by an PA DEP OGI during an inspection conducted on 12/15/2023 (Sub-SAIR# 3660126). At the time of inspection, the following was observed:Act 9 Sign Installed, however the Operator of Record does not appear to be correct. The associated PPC plan and ER plan on site have not been updated to reflect the change in ownership. (Photo 11 and 12)The COASTAL Drill Rig was on site and connected to the well. The drill rig and associated equipment was not placed within secondary containment. (Photo 1)I observed fluid on the well pad surrounding the WL Hopkins 590312 Well and drill rig. I also observed fluid within the well cellar. I collected conductivity readings of the fluid on the well pad and within the cellar, which result in elevated conductivity readings. I also observed what appeared to be a light colored crystallin substance deposited on the well pad rock adjacent to the standing fluid. The crystallin substance appears to be salt which suggest that the fluid has been on site long enough to begin evaporation. The amount of fluid on the well pad appeared to be greater than 42 gallons. At the time of inspection, the Department was not previously notified by the Operator of a release of fluid to the well pad. (Photo 2 thru 10)While I was on site, I contacted Operator representative Kevin Wright (CONSOL/Leatherwood) to relay my observations related to the fluid release and recommend that the Operator being remediation immediately. Mr. Wright indicated that the Operator added brine to the well to kill the well on 11/15/2023.I am requesting clarification of the activity, date and time of when the fluid was added to the well bore and all information/inspections related to the monitoring of the well between 11/15/2023 and 12/15/2023. I am also requesting clarification of the source of the fluid added to the well bore on or around 11/15/2023.Violation are being issued for the release (78a.54, 78a57(a), 91.34(a), SWMA 301, 78a66(b)1,78a(b)1(i), 78a66(b)1(ii), 78a66(b)(2), 91.33(a) and 91.33(b).Violations are being issued for the failure to develop a site specific PPC plan and ER Plan. 78a55(a), 78a55(b), 78a55(c). 78a55(h).Violations are being issued for the failure to properly update the Act 9 Sign (78a55(i)(4)(D)(III).Violations are being issued for the failure to install secondary containment. (78a64(a))

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PENNHILLS RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/15/2022
Violation Code: SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
Violation ID: 948071
Permit API: 083-49666
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Hamilton Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/15/2022
Comments: This inspection was performed following a report of an oil and gas leak in the vicinity of Chappel Fork near the road crossing of RT 321 (CTS #362745). At the time of the report to DEP, I spoke to the complainant and determined the location to begin searching. I contacted Pennhills Resources as they have wells in the immediate vicinity, and we agreed to meet on site to look. After beginning at Rt 321 we headed east until we found some oil collected in a low spot. It appears as though a line has burst with some gas pressure on the line, causing oil and gas to bubble to the surface. The oil then flowed south and into a low swale, where the majority of it collected. Some crude then flowed through into a channel formed by the collection of two spring runs, and toward the main branch of Chappel Fork. Oil was collecting behind ice pockets and in between leaves and dead vegetation for approximately 200 feet. A small amount of sheen was noted in Chappel Fork, but no free product. Approximately 15-20 barrels of oil was emitted from the line in total. Another small area nearer to the creek when following the line was noted to contain some basic sediment and paraffin at the surface and under a hemlock tree; it is uncertain if this is another leak site or simply product following the line. Pennhills immediately moved to contain the spill with booms in the back channel, and then brought a mini excavator to site to dig up the line and slow the leak. The 2" line was uncovered and a band placed on the line, which was broken on the bottom. It was determined that the old access past well 9A could be used to mobilize equipment and some brush was removed to make for better access. A vac truck was brought to site to collect any free product available, which was able to get a large amount on the first load. It was determined the evening of 3/15 that the line belonged to Pennhills, who will be continuing to clean up the oil and soil until clean. The operator built two underflow dams to contain any free product flowing down the channel with melting ice starting to give way. Followup inspection will be performed as necessary.

Comments: This well was inspected as part of an ongoing investigation into stray gas migration, involving combustible gas detected at the foundation of a nearby private residence. Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 2/07/2024
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection at Repsol's Crank O (03-067) well site located in Columbia Township, Bradford County on 2/7/2024 at 1025 hours. The weather was 35 degrees F with partly cloudy skies. The inspection was conducted in response to a release reported to the DEP by Repsol. Complaint Tracking System (CTS) ID #378016 is tied to the release in CTS.According to Repsol, on 2/4/2024 at 0840 hours, a spill of approximately 15 gallons of hydraulic fluid was released to the pad surface after a hose on a water truck was found to be leaking. Repsol reported that the release was cleaned up utilizing absorbents and the impacted pad material was recovered and placed in containers for disposal. Repsol reported that no waterways were impacted by the release. During today's inspection, no evidence of any portion of the release remaining could be observed. An environmental consultant was onsite today for proper disposal/removal of the impacted material from the site. Repsol is currently moving equipment offsite and preparing for a workover rig to move in. Silt sock and a gravel berm were installed along the southwestern edge of the pad for sedimentation control (photo #2). Areas surrounding the well pad remain permanently stabilized with vegetated cover or temporarily stabilized with straw. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation was observed. No pooled water was observed on the pad surface, outside of secondary containment today.Based on the reported release of ~15 gallons of hydraulic fluid to the pad surface and Repsol's timely remediation of the release, violations of the following are cited as immediately corrected against API #015-23837:CSL 402(b)25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)SWMA 301The 25 Pa. Code 78a.64a(e) violation cited against API #015-23837 on 1/30/2024 remains outstanding at this time.I departed the site at 1100 hours.

There did not appear to be a recent flow path of fluid in the section of ditch from the last location of standing water to the remainder of ditch before the stream. No sheen, discoloration, or foaming was observed in the stream. It does not appear from the observations and readings that there was a release into Waters of the Commonwealth.The Department recommends the operator promptly install/implement temporary erosion and sediment controls. The Department also recommends the operator temporarily stabilize any disturbed areas with in 4 days following cessation of earth disturbance activities.Based on today's inspection, violation remain outstanding as a notice of intent to conduct Act 2 remediation has not yet been received by the Department.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CNX GAS CO LLC

Violation Date: 11/05/2025
Violation Code: 78a65(a)1i - SITE RESTORATION - Post Drilling - Owner or operator failed to restore the land surface within 9 months after completion of drilling all permitted wells on the well site or 9 months after the expiration of all existing well permits on the well site, whichever is later.
Violation ID: 8255530
Permit API: 129-29261
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Sewickley Township
Inspection Type: Site Restoration
Inspection Date: 11/05/2025
Comments: On November 5, 2025, the DEP conducted a Restoration Inspection of CNX's Herminie Well Site (ESG076523008-00) located in Sewickley Township, Westmoreland County following a Post-Drilling Site Restoration Report (PDSRR) submission the DEP received on 10/17/2025 (Final well drilled: 129-29261 Drilling Completed on: 1/30/2025.) In accordance with 78a.65, within 9 months after the completion of drilling a well or expiration of the permit for the last well drilled, the Operator shall restore the well site. 9 months after the completion of drilling for the last well drilled at the Herminie Well Site is 10/30/2025. At the time of this inspection the DEP observed the Act 9 sign at the access road entrance with all required information posted on it. In the onsite mailbox, the DEP observed a Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan as well as an Emergency Response Plan both with all required components. At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed an access road that was stabilized with gravel, to the right of the access road entrance, the DEP observed an infiltration basin and outlet. The basin and outlet appeared to be constructed and functioning according to PCSM plans, however, the outlet was not observed to be exhibiting 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth and Compost Filter Sock (CFS) was observed to still be installed at the infiltration basin outlet.At the time of this inspection, a soil stockpile located adjacent to the access road was observed to be exhibiting at least 70% vegetative cover, however, CFS was observed to still be installed around the base of the stockpile.At the time of this inspection, a second infiltration basin was observed to be located adjacent to the access road, this basin and its outlet were observed to be constructed and functioning according to PCSM plans, however, CFS was observed to still be installed around the infiltration basin outlet.At the time of this inspection, the South Perimeter of the well pad and a soil stockpile located adjacent to the well pad was observed to be exhibiting less than 70% vegetative cover, however, it was observed to be thoroughly seeded/mulched. A third infiltration basin and outlet was observed adjacent to the well pad on the south perimeter, these features appeared to be constructed and functioning according to PCSM plans, however, they too were exhibiting less than 70% vegetative cover and had CFS installed around the basin and outlet.At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed the other perimeters of the well pad to be nearing the 70% vegetative cover requirement and CFS was observed to be installed at the edge of the perimeters. Included in the Limit of Disturbance for this site, is a smaller gravel pad. The perimeters of this gravel pad and its access road were observed to be exhibiting less than 70% vegetative growth and were thoroughly seeded and mulched with CFS installed on the perimeter edges. At the time of this inspection, the DEP did not observe any drilling equipment not necessary for production to be located on the well site. Based on today's inspection, it appears the Herminie well site is not meeting the requirements set forth in 78a.65 Site Restoration, therefore the DEP is recommending the PDSRR Submission be denied. The Department recommends the Operator resubmit a PDSRR upon complete restoration of the Herminie well site in accordance with 78a.65.Based on today's inspection, violations shall be issued for failure to restore the well site within 9 months of the completion of the final well.

properties.content:
Report Details

Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Wyalusing Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/08/2023
Comments: On 6/8/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a routine site inspection at the Chesapeake Solowiej well site. It was 65 degrees and mostly clear when I arrived on location. I did not screen for conductivity because I did not witness any water puddles or muddy areas on the pad surface during the inspection.No E and S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. The site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. PCSM is addressed by one sediment pond. The sediment pond is adequately stabilized and was dry at the time of the inspection. I was able to witness an 8 inch riser sticking up about 16 inches from the pond surface. The outlet for the sediment pond overflow drains into a stream alongside the River View roadway. This stream drains to the waters of the Commonwealth. Following an inspection conducted on 10/18/2022, Chesapeake reported that it would make changes to the site to mitigate the issues with the sediment pond. They reported that they were developing a design to accommodate both the drainage and the land owner and hoped to have a finalized plan with the proper drainage and post construction stormwater features. There are outstanding violations against the outfall coming off the sediment pond. There were three wells staged for production. All wells were tagged with API/well permit numbers. No bubbling within the cellars was observed. The production tank had secondary containment.The DEP recommends that Chesapeake continues with the process to obtain a revised ESCGP application with the proper drainage and post construction stormwater features and submit to the Department for review.I left the site at 1400 hours.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RUSS HOLDEN WELL SVC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/14/2026
Violation Code: 78.53 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL - Operator failed to design, implement and maintain best management practices and an erosion and sediment control plan in accordance with 25 Pa. Code Chapter 102, during and after earthmoving or soil disturbing activities, including the activities related to siting, drilling, completing, producing, servicing and plugging, constructing, utilizing and restoring the site and access road.
Violation ID: 8288773
Permit API: 123-47965
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Watson Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/14/2026
Comments: I conducted a routine inspection of this conventional well. Road work had recently taken place on a section from the Lot 545 #24 well to the Lot 545 #19 well and down to the Lot 545 #20 well. The work done has not improved the condition of the road and has worsened it. Tail ditches were installed but are above the road bed, significant soft soil is also creating berms at the edge of the road preventing the water from reach tail ditches. As a consequence the water is still running directly down the road and not making it into the ditches or installed BMPs. The road itself needs a proper crown to allow run off to get into the ditches and/or tail ditches. The road is extremely soft and muddy between the two previously mentioned wells. The road leading towards Lot 545 #24 is also very deteriorated due to lack of maintenance and improperly crowned roads. This has led to accelerated erosion and sedimentation. The poor road conditions start at the turn off for the lease, just above Slater Run (an EV designated stream) and continue across Slater Run and continue on into the Lot 545 lease. The whole road system needs properly crowned and road ditches to be reestablished where they have failed. Run off is observed running on the road while the road ditches remain dry.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/21/2022
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 989362
Permit API: 015-23708
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Asylum Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/21/2023
Comments: On 3/21/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an incident - response to an accident or event inspection at the Chesapeake Hopson well site. On 3/18/2023 Chesapeake reported that 10 gallons of produced water sprayed out of a damaged pipe on a GPU unit, the water impacting the unprotected pad surface. Creston Environmental identified the extent of the impacted area and excavation was scheduled for 3/20/2023. It was 39 degrees and clear when I arrived on location.When I first arrived at the site, I met Chesapeake's Pat Adams who described activities with the event. Pat showed me a pipe nipple on the 1HC GPU that had been replaced. He showed me the excavated area that is in the northeast corner of the site. The excavated hole had not been backfilled at the time of the inspection. The excavated area is roughly 12' x 40' with various depths up to 2', running along the edge of the perimeter berm. The GPU had been moved from the affected area and had not been returned back to its original position. Pat said that a truck driver first witnessed the spill. Upon discovery, all ten wells were shut in. Pat had just put the 9 unaffected wells back into production before my arrival. The 1HC was still shut in until the GPU is reinstalled. The excavated material remains on site and has been piled on a plastic sheet on the southeast corner of the pad. I field tested some small water puddles in the bottom of the excavated area with results being as high as 4.18 mS conductance. Using a Hanna Gro-line soil probe, I probed the side of the excavated area with one reading being 1.03 mS conductance. I discussed the elevated conductance of the water and soil with Chesapeake's Eric Hottenstein. Eric said he would have someone probe the excavated area to determine if further excavation was necessary. Eric also reported that it was their practice not to fill in the excavated area until they had gotten confirmation samples back. Danielle Schaad met me on location before I left and we discussed the elevated conductance areas. She said that they would excavate some more of the area as determined by the results of field tests.There were nine wells staged for production and one offline at the time of the inspection. All wells were tagged with API/well permit numbers. No bubbling within the cellars was observed. Six of the GPUs and the production tank had secondary containment. Water in the 101HC GPU secondary containment field tested at 4.55 mS conductance. There are seven frac tanks on site along with one gas buster that were located in secondary containment. Pat reported that the wells were sending their production fluid directly to the production tank. He said the frac tanks were not being used but were still on site in case of inclement weather.No E and S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. Most of the site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. Temporary stabilization was noted on the east perimeter berm. PCSM is addressed by two retentive grading/infiltration areas that are adequately stabilized and functioning as designed.This spill constitutes violations of these three regulations; 78a 57(a), SWMA 301, and CSL 402(b). Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3459318 for the spill of brine fluid outside of secondary containment.The DEP recommends the following:1. Screen the area impacted by the release of production fluid for additional contaminants and continue with the excavation as determined by the screening results.2. Remove the water in the 101HC GPU secondary containment at the earliest convenience.I left the site at 1335 hours.

Unconventional: Yes
County: Wyoming
Municipality: Windham Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection

Comments: At time of inspection, 32 degs. and cloudy. There is (1) well on this pad, the Warren 2H, it was in production at time of inspection. The (9x5) and the (13x9) annulus vents are plumbed to surface w/ 2" pipe and "T"'d into a 2" common pipe venting to the prod. tanks. The (20x13) annulus is venting to atmosphere via Sentry valve. The (9x5) and (13x9) annulus vents are open. There was gas previously detected in the (20x13) annulus. Outside the surface casing. No gas was detected @ Sentry valve during this inspection. - The cellar had water in it w/ no bubbling observed during insp. An ALTAIR 5X gas meter (cal. 3/5/21) was turned on at well head to check for gas at Sentry valve and left on during walk around pad and prod. equipment. No gas was detected in ambient air. - Individual well pressures listed below were all taken off digital SCADA gauges. - 2H - prod. tree top press.: 1,158.4 psi., prod. csg. press.: 59.7 psi., (9x5) annulus press.: 1.0 psi, (13x9) annulus press.: 1.9 psi., (20 x13) annulus press.: 0.0 psi. and prod. line press.: 1,199 psi. - There is self contained ancillary equipment on site. - There are (2) well slots on pad, the one closest to the 2H is plugged(5H) and (1) well slot is open. - No obvious concerns or new violations noted.

Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga

Inspection Date: 9/25/2025
Comments: At time of inspection: On site for a P and A inspection for the Phoenix 590796 (117-20970) well. I met with EQT Rep., Doug Fry and Moody Rep., Jon Hafer. I will conduct a post-plugging inspection after monitoring is completed.
